newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end with slim gain, seen wary.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end with slim gain, seen wary.

text.p: Argentine stocks recorded slim gains at the close Monday but may struggle to keep their positive edge, dealers said.

"I don't think the uptick will last because nobody seems willing to take a risk," said Gabriel Armando at brokers Galicia Valores. "Political rows are still hurting sentiment and there's very few players in the market."
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.5 percent to close at 562.22. The MerVal pulled back 4.0 percent in the past two weeks and shows a narrow gain so far in October.
Technical analysts said the MerVal might find resistance as near as 565-570.

"Very few people are bullish short-term. And I'd say it's not just about (the political row in) Argentina but about the run-up to the U.S. elections and the situation in countries like Brazil and Mexico," said an analyst at a foreign-based investment bank. "In New York the talk again is about the economy and what the Fed will do after the elections."
The U.S. Federal Reserve meets November 13 to discuss interest rates and traders said a raft of economic indicators due this week could help hint at its likely action.
At home investors remained concerned over lingering political tension related to allegations of government-linked corruption made two weeks ago by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.
The bolsa's broad market index in the session matched the MerVal's 0.5 percent gain, with winners whipping losers 25 to nine and 23 issues closing flat.
Floor volume remained dismally low at 10.7 million pesos compared to 10.4 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals swelled to 91.4 million pesos from 55.2 million Friday.
The day's top main-tier gainers were steelmaker Siderca, footwear and textile firm Alpargatas and Bansud bank, which advanced 3.4 percent, 1.8 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively.

The only MerVal losers carmaker Sevel, which dropped 2.4 percent, gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, off 1.3 percent, and steelmaker Acindar and holding company Perez Companc, both off 0.5 percent.
Traders said investors would continue to track the performance of the markets in Brazil and Mexico.
